lessons: Do not play 15 cheap ground creatures without fliers: my WG with two Voiceless Spirits, Abbey Griffin and Somberwald Spiders still lost 1-2 to a WG that won with Festerhide Boar and Lumberknot, so draft a third evasive threat over a Villagers copy.
Your guide's BG/WG advice is incomplete: my WG went 1-2 against UB and WG, losing 15 and 11 turn games, so take Victim of Night or Dead Weight early and count fliers before ground filler.

The guide's 'take a third flier over a second Unruly Mob' advice held, but I took Villagers of Estwald third and Grave Bramble early, so commit to Spidery Grasp and Blazing Torch removal and keep a 10th-source main colour.
I took Olivia Voldaren second, then left her out of my black deck while playing Butcher's Cleaver and Geistcatcher's Rig; play the bomb and cut the equipment first.
I lost 1-2 to WU fliers (Geist of Saint Traft, Moon Heron) with few cheap answers, so take flier-answering removal like Silent Departure and Sever the Bloodline earlier.
Blue-black creatures kept flowing (second Stitched Drake and two Rotting Fensnakes came late), so once the bodies are covered, prioritise removal over more bodies.
Don't hedge with Brimstone Volley: I took two in pack 2 while firmly WU, wasting picks that on-colour fliers or removal would have filled; commit by mid-pack 2.
Blazing Torch, colourless removal the guide ranks highly, never made my deck, and WU lacked cheap answers to the three Tormented Pariah that beat me 2-1 in round 3.
Games ran 13 to 34 turns, so a sixteen-creature low curve needed late-game power and finishers, not just cheap bodies, to close out Round 3's grindy UB deck.
Against Round 3's Stitched Drake and Delver of Secrets, my green-white deck lacked enough flying defence and reach, so take flyer answers before extra two-drops.
Mulch and Spidery Grasp were filler; prioritise Boneyard Wurm-style value creatures and removal over tricks that only matter in combat.
The guide's UB warnings held: my UB went 1-2 (2-5 in games) while running Delver of Secrets and Markov Patrician, both listed as skips, so leave them out and take a flier instead.
Against RG's Balefire Dragon, my UB had one Claustrophobia and one Sensory Deprivation and lost 0-2 in 18 and 22 turns; take a second flier answer before pack 3.
Plan for long games: my 3-5 record came in 15-to-51-turn matches, so Moan of the Unhallowed and Stensia Bloodhall deserve more value than my quick-aggro notes assumed.

I lost 0-2 to the WG deck with Somberwald Spider, three Villagers of Estwald and Travel Preparations after my small BR creatures stalled, so prioritize removal and bigger bodies over Reckless Waif-type 1-drops.
Brimstone Volley never showed up, so Harvest Pyre was my only real red removal; I took it fourth in pack 1 and second in pack 2, and it stayed in the deck. Take it early.
The guide calls Festerhide Boar filler, but it made my 3-0 deck. I also ran 17 lands where it suggests 16 for aggro, and the mana was fine, so 17 is a reasonable default.
Tormented Pariah carried the werewolf plan: I took three at picks 2, 5 and 9 of pack 3, alongside Darkthicket Wolf. Prioritise werewolves over vanilla two-drops in RG.
Blue-black self-mill built on Skaab Ruinator and Stitcher's Apprentice stretched Round 2 games to 51 and 29 turns against BR, so add a faster clock or more evasive threats.
Round 1's RG Tormented Pariah aggro beat me 2-1, so prioritize cheap interaction like Sensory Deprivation and early blockers over late-game card advantage.
My only match win was 2-0 against UB, while RG aggro and BR attrition took the other two matches, so draft the early curve before the late-game engines.
